relevance.rationale: Identified from front matter as a 1995 Miami preprint (q-alg/9504015, report UMTG-183-95) by L. Rozansky relating the coefficients of the asymptotic expansion of the trivial-connection contribution to Witten's invariant of rational homology spheres to Ohtsuki's invariants extracted at prime K, and proving Ohtsuki's invariants are of finite type. Supporting rather than core: it supplies the machinery and the literature warrant for reading a perturbative Chern-Simons expansion as the Ohtsuki series, which is the framing the keystone's Beasley-Witten localization route assumes, but the corpus consumes no result of this paper today and none of its statements discharges a named obligation. Citation status checked all three ways: no ref() id (the only Rozansky among the 481 registered ids is khovanov-rozansky2008, a different author-pair and a different subject), no cite{} in content/**/*.md, no '-- Ref:' in content/**/*.lean, and a grep for '9504015' across content/, docs/ and computations/ returns only the ledger row. Deliberately NOT proposed as aid-proof: QOU/BraidKnot/KeystoneRTSurgeryConstruction.lean carries the RT/WRT = Chern-Simons partition-function identification as an explicit named hypothesis, and this paper does not discharge it — Proposition 1.1 concerns only the trivial-connection sector of the asymptotic expansion, not the full finite-K identification, and its Seifert verification is a check rather than a Kirby-move-invariance proof. Scope-(a) on the two gaps it does not touch: this document, as read, supplies nothing bearing on the corpus's 5_2 DT-spectrum data or on the GGM Stokes-conjecture attribution, both of which concern non-perturbative Stokes constants of knot state integrals rather than the perturbative 3-manifold sector treated here.

keyResults.locator: Proposition 1.1, p. 5 (proved in Section 3; verified for lens spaces and Seifert manifolds in Section 4)
keyResults.statement: Ohtsuki's invariants lambda_n(M) and the loop corrections S_n(M) to the trivial-connection contribution determine each other through sum_n lambda_n(M) x^n = exp[ sum_{n>=1} (S_n(M) - S_n(S^3)) (i pi/K)^n ] evaluated at x = exp(2 pi i/K) - 1, with S_1(M) = 6 lambda_CW.
keyResults.useForFolio: Gives the keystone's Chern-Simons framing its literature warrant at exactly the manifold class it needs: the identification is verified in Section 4 for Seifert manifolds, the class containing S^3/2I = Sigma(2,3,5). It says the perturbative expansion of a localized CS partition function on that manifold is the exponential of the connected loop corrections whose resummation is the Ohtsuki series — the step the Beasley-Witten route (#2524) takes for granted.

keyResults.statement: The Kirby-Melvin surgery formula for Z'(M;k) as a sum over odd colours of the framing-independent coloured Jones polynomial weighted by prod_j sin(pi alpha_j/K); and, for the Seifert surgery link of N unknots linked to a single unknot, the explicit sine-product coloured Jones J_{beta,alpha_1..alpha_N}(L;k) = prod_j sin(pi beta alpha_j/K) / [sin^{N-1}(pi beta/K) sin(pi/K)] up to normalisation.
keyResults.useForFolio: The per-colour weight sin(pi alpha/K) is the S-matrix vacuum row d_alpha/D that KeystoneRTSurgeryConstruction.lean proves the RT surgery sum weights each label by — so (1.6) is an explicit analytic instance of the assembly that file formalises abstractly. Equation (4.28) then gives the coloured Seifert link invariant in closed sine-product form, which is the machinery the colored-Sigma(2,3,5) step needs to lift the bare closed-manifold number to a lambda-indexed family. Useful as a cited construction to build against; it is not a substitute for the carried (RT) hypothesis.

proposedActions.rationale: Orphan with no ref() entry, and the corpus currently registers no Lev-Rozansky 3-manifold source at all despite the keystone ledger repeatedly invoking Lawrence-Rozansky as '(LR)'. Metadata in references.ts only.

KeystoneRTSurgeryConstruction.lean carries the RT/WRT = Chern-Simons identification as a named, cited-but-unformalised hypothesis whose '-- Ref:' list currently names only Reshetikhin-Turaev 1991 / Turaev 1994 and beasleywitten2005. Adding this paper documents the perturbative form of that identification and its explicit verification on the Seifert class the file's manifold belongs to, so a reader can see how far the cited literature actually goes. It documents the hypothesis; it does not discharge it, and the file's honest-scope banner should stay unchanged.
